title: Restricting AI agents in mobile operating systems platforms from capturing data
lede: Signal will block screen capture on iOS 27 and on Android when it detects an AI assistant reading the screen, to keep OS-level agents from harvesting message content.

points: It extends the screenshot blocking Signal added against Microsoft Recall on Windows 11.
Agents such as Gemini on Android and Siri's onscreen awareness capture screen content and pass it to their own storage and servers.
On Android, Signal turns on its Screen security setting automatically when assistant access is detected; users can disable the protection.
macOS is not covered because Apple offers no reliable way to block screenshots, and filesystem access remains open everywhere.
Signal asks Apple, Google and Microsoft for a documented app opt-out from AI data access and clear specifications of how agents work.

points.text: Commenters note that blocking your own device is not enough: a contact with an AI-enabled phone still exposes the chat.
One commenter wants Signal to call these systems spyware and point users to GrapheneOS; a reply notes Signal does not officially support it.
Some resent losing screenshots on Windows as a basic feature, while others question how a desktop app can enforce that at all.
Much of the thread turns to older complaints: phone-number accounts, no anonymous payment option, and captchas behind VPNs.
